Memory items from past tasks:
- [rb-0014] Validate numeric inputs via Decimal(str(x)) with explicit bool rejection: Convert user-supplied rates through Decimal(str(value)) and reject bools, catching InvalidOperation/ValueError to raise the domain error.
  Booleans are ints in Python, so check isinstance(x, bool) first. Wrapping Decimal(str(x)) in try/except (InvalidOperation, ValueError) handles strings, None, and other junk uniformly, then range-check the Decimal before computing.
- [rb-0006] Read existing modules to match error conventions: Before implementing, inspect errors.py and sibling modules to reuse the project's BillingError codes and helper functions.
  Explore the repo's error class and existing functions first; reuse established error codes (e.g. invalid_state, invalid_quantity, negative_amount) and helpers rather than inventing new ones. This keeps behavior consistent with hidden tests.
- [rb-0019] Match sibling module conventions before implementing: Reading existing modules (payments.py, money.py, errors.py) revealed the exact validation pattern and error code to reuse.
  Before writing a new function, grep for similar operations in sibling modules and copy their validation/error conventions (e.g. BillingError('non_positive_amount', str(amount))). Hidden tests often assert on these exact codes and helpers.
- [rb-0001] Reuse existing money helpers for Decimal arithmetic: When implementing monetary calculations, use the project's existing money utilities (to_money, round_money, ZERO) rather than raw Decimal operations.
  Inspect ledgerly/money.py and sibling functions like line_total/invoice_total to match rounding and normalization conventions. Wrap unit prices with to_money, seed sums with ZERO, and round the final result with round_money.
- [rb-0002] Guard division by zero with the domain's zero constant: For weighted-average or ratio computations, check the denominator (total quantity) before dividing and return the project's ZERO constant.
  Compute total_quantity first; if it equals 0 (empty invoice or zero-quantity lines), return ZERO instead of raising ZeroDivisionError. This satisfies the 'no lines means zero' requirement cleanly.
- [rb-0003] Read the existing test file before implementing: Locating and reading the relevant test file (tests/test_average_unit_price.py) alongside models.py and money.py clarified expected types and behavior before writing code.
  Before editing, cat the target module, its models, its money helpers, and any test file matching the feature name. This reveals signatures, Decimal usage, and edge cases, enabling a first-attempt pass.

item.title: Reuse existing money helpers instead of reimplementing rounding
item.description: The repo already provides to_money and round_money in ledgerly/money.py; the accepted solution composed them rather than writing new Decimal conversion/rounding logic.
item.content: Before implementing numeric logic, grep for existing helpers (to_money, round_money, ZERO, CENT) and build on them. This keeps rounding semantics (ROUND_HALF_EVEN) and validation consistent with the rest of the codebase.

item.title: Validate rates with Decimal(str(x)) and reject bools/non-finite
item.description: The accepted _to_rate converts via Decimal(str(rate_percent)), rejects bool explicitly, catches InvalidOperation/ValueError, checks is_finite, then enforces the 0-50 bounds.
item.content: For percentage/rate inputs, mirror money.py's pattern: reject bool first, use Decimal(str(value)) inside try/except (InvalidOperation, ValueError), reject non-finite values, then range-check. Raise the project's BillingError with a short code like 'invalid_rate'.

item.title: Read sibling modules and existing tests to infer conventions
item.description: The agent inspected errors.py, money.py, payments.py, and tests/test_commissions.py before writing code, matching error codes, imports, and expected return types.
item.content: Start each task by reading the target module's stub, its test file, and 2-3 sibling modules. This reveals the error class/codes, helper functions, and expected Decimal return types so the first attempt matches hidden tests.
